summary: Pinned-session entropy and route reversion after partial canary rollback
description:
Issue summary: After a partial canary rollback initiated for redwood-7b-v1.2, a subset of tenant sessions that had pinned model versions experienced route reversion to a legacy variant and intermittent mixed responses. Impact: customer saw mixed model outputs for live sessions, some requests routed to an older variant without pin being explicitly changed. Environment: production (dedicated) in us-east-1 for NimbleScribe. Observed starting 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC during canary rollback window.

Expected behavior: pinned sessions should retain their pinned variant during rollbacks, or fall back deterministically to configured fallback policy. Actual behavior: a cohort (~0.8% of active sessions for the tenant) lost pin affinity and were routed to legacy variant (llama2-13b-quant), producing inconsistent outputs and causing a short-term quality regression for customer traffic.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start with tenant using pinned model redwood-7b-v1.2.
2) Initiate canary promote to redwood-7b-v1.3 for 10% traffic, wait for health probes.
3) Run partial rollback to revert canary at 09:58 UTC (abort promote, commit rollback).
4) Observe session affinity map and edge headers for affected tenant cohort.
5) Reproduce by replaying traffic from recorded session IDs through edge (see attached session list).

comments: 2026-03-10 09:20 Support (Maya): Customer reported mixed model outputs after canary rollback; attached sample request/response pairs.

2026-03-10 09:40 Eng (Liam): Initial hypothesis: edge health-probe or sidecar header sanitizer stripped X-Redwood-Pin during in-flight rollback commit, causing routing to recompute and select fallback variant.
2026-03-10 10:05 Customer (NimbleScribe): Confirmed roughly 0.6-1.0% of requests returned legacy outputs; business impact limited but visible in QA channel.
2026-03-10 14:02 Eng (SRE - Priya): Found control-plane snapshot merge ordering warnings around rollback commit. Prepared quick mitigation to reapply pin on active sessions.

2026-03-12 02:14 Eng (Liam): Patch deployed to reconciler and edge-sidecar to preserve pin headers during health-probes and enforce commit serial ordering. Backfilled pins for affected sessions. Monitoring shows no further regressions.
investigation:
Timeline reconstruction shows a narrow window where three events coincided: (1) operator-initiated partial rollback commit on control-plane, (2) a burst of health-checks hitting edge sidecars which triggered header sanitizer rule, and (3) control-plane snapshot merge code applied snapshots out-of-order for ephemeral commit IDs. Logs show 'commit-order-mismatch' warning immediately before edge removed X-Redwood-Pin for a subset of sessions. Session lease renewal traces indicated delayed lease refresh due to reconciler holding a lock while merging snapshots. The combination produced transient entropy in the routing decision: sessions without X-Redwood-Pin were evaluated by route-engine and matched fallback variant ruleset that selected a legacy model.

Hypotheses tested: header-stripping during health probes (confirmed), reconciler commit-ordering race (reproducible in staging with canary scripts), session lease TTL renewal delay under lock (observed in traces).
root_cause: A race during partial canary rollback where control-plane snapshot merge applied snapshots with commit-order mismatch while edge-sidecar health-probe sanitization removed pin headers for requests. The reconciler's commit application path temporarily blocked lease renewals, leading to pin eviction for a small session cohort. Combined, this produced non-deterministic routing and fallback to legacy variants.
mitigation:
Immediate: re-applied pin metadata for affected tenant sessions from control-plane snapshot backups and forced lease renewal. Added a temporary rule to disable header sanitizer for X-Redwood-Pin during rollback windows.
Medium-term: deployed reconciler patch to enforce strict commit-serial application and prevent snapshot reorders. Deployed edge-sidecar patch to treat X-Redwood-Pin as protected header (not removed by health-probe sanitizer). Added metrics/alert to detect header removals and commit-order warnings.
actions_taken:
2026-03-10 11:20 UTC: Reapplied pins for 142 affected session IDs (script: tools/reapply_pins.sh --tenant nimble-123 --file sessions.csv).
2026-03-10 13:45 UTC: Disabled legacy header sanitizer rule in prod for edge cluster us-east-1.
2026-03-11 22:30 UTC: Reconciler patch merged and rolled to canary (PR #4203).
2026-03-12 02:10 UTC: Edge-sidecar patch rolled (PR #3891) and protected header behavior enabled.
resolution_notes: Patch to control-plane reconciler and edge-sidecar released. Backfill script reapplied pins and forced lease renewals. Customer confirmed that mixed outputs stopped within one hour of mitigation. Monitoring dashboards show no recurrence for 48 hours post-deploy. Ticket marked Resolved pending postmortem follow-ups.
postmortem_followups: Add an automated integration test that simulates canary rollback + health-probe storms to catch header-preservation regressions.
Instrument 'X-Redwood-Pin' header removal with a dedicated metric and alert threshold (SLO: zero removals during rollouts).
Revise runbook: during rollback operations, disable aggressive header sanitization rules or run sanitizer after pin re-assertion step.
Consider reducing lock duration in reconciler snapshot merge path and introduce async lease refresh where safe.
related_fix_release: 2026-03-11: reconciler v2.8.4-canary -> 2026-03-12 full rollout reconciler v2.8.4, edge-sidecar v1.12.1
notes_for_customer: We re-applied pinned-model state for affected sessions and deployed fixes to prevent header stripping and commit reordering. We will run a post-change verification on next scheduled canary and share the test run results. If you see any further anomalies, please open a new ticket and include sample request_ids.
